title: Live OEE dashboard for a 3-machine CNC cell (example data)
summary: A fictional 18:00 snapshot with raw counts, reproducible OEE and an honest loss breakdown.

blocks.title: One number per machine, three numbers behind it
blocks.body: Static example at 18:00 for a shift starting at 15:00. Each machine has 180 planned minutes and a fictional ideal cycle of 1 minute per part. The page does not update from machines. Counts and elapsed times below produce every displayed OEE figure.

items.label: Cell OEE: 345 good ideal minutes / 540 planned

blocks.heading: Machine totals at 18:00
blocks.caption: All data invented. Ratios are calculated from raw counts before rounding. Common 1 min/part ideal cycle permits this simple aggregation.

blocks.heading: How each number is earned
blocks.body: Availability = run minutes / planned minutes. Performance = ideal cycle × total parts / run minutes. Quality = first-pass good / total parts. Multiplying cancels the intermediate denominators: cell OEE = 345 / 540 = 63.888…%. Do not multiply rounded display percentages and expect the exact total. Different ideal cycles require a correctly weighted aggregation.

blocks.heading: Where the 195 lost ideal minutes went
blocks.caption: These three categories are mutually exclusive in this model. Asset-specific root-cause claims need event-level evidence.

items.title: Mill 3 operator reports chatter
items.detail: Observed symptom; tool, setup and quality records need review before declaring a root cause.

items.title: Mill 2 stops for a probe issue
items.detail: 23 minutes of its 35 stopped minutes; 12 minutes came from earlier recorded stops.

items.title: Snapshot
items.detail: All three machines running. Mill 3 has the largest loss of good ideal production minutes.

blocks.heading: How to operate on this board
items: Read the cell number, then immediately read the three factors - a low OEE with high availability is a different animal than one with low availability.
Read the machine state and the raw counts; Mill 3’s largest category is cycle loss, which still needs investigation.
Check the losses table against the story: does the biggest loss have an owner and a date?
Act on one loss per shift. Boards that spawn five action items spawn none.

blocks.title: What this board cannot tell you
blocks.body: OEE says nothing about whether the cell is running the right parts, whether the schedule itself is sane, or whether the ideal rates are honest. An 85% OEE on work nobody ordered is worse than 55% on the hot job. The number starts the conversation; it is never the conversation's end.
